Hi Tom —

Appreciate the precise questions. Quick summary up front: egress is enforced at the tenant VPC/subnet boundary via managed egress gateways (per-tenant allow-lists) and we do not permit unrestricted host-level outbound connections from tenant compute. Support access uses a dedicated management plane (separate VPC/VLAN) with just-in-time (JIT) bastion provisioning and ephemeral keys; we never leave persistent admin shells in tenant subnets.

I've attached a high-level diagram (deployment-egress-diagram.svg) and a 2-pg controls summary (egress-rules-summary.pdf). Below are the short answers you can share with the audit team; I'll coordinate a walkthrough Monday AM.

Egress enforcement (short):
- Enforcement point: per-tenant egress gateway at the VPC/subnet level. Gateways are policy-driven; tenant requests are NATed through the gateway, which applies allow-lists and TLS inspection where required.
- Host-level restrictions: node/container firewall rules restrict outbound to only the egress gateway IP; kernel-level network policies and container runtime deny policy prevent direct external sockets.

Bastion / support access (short):
- Management plane: Dedicated management VPC with peering through an audited transit network; support sessions are brokered through JIT bastion instances that are ephemeral (TTL 15–120 minutes).
- Authentication & audit: JIT requests require SSO + MFA and are recorded; session recordings, keystroke logging, and live command audit are stored in immutable logs (retention policy configurable per-customer).

Threat mapping document: attached is a concise mapping in the controls PDF; if you prefer I can expand it into a one-page attack-path table.

Next: I propose a 30-min walkthrough Monday 2027-04-12 09:00–09:30 PT. Does that work?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Solutions Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Tom / Acme team —

Thanks for the original note. Per Mark's suggested clarifications (included below) and the attachments, here is a consolidated response you can include in the audit packet. I've embedded the key facts and fail-safe behaviors to address the audit criteria.

[Consolidated technical response — shareable excerpt]
1) Enforcement point and granularity
- Egress is enforced at the tenant VPC/subnet boundary via an L3+ managed egress gateway; all tenant compute traffic to external destinations is NATed through the gateway. Host/container runtime rules prevent direct outbound sockets to prevent bypass.
- Per-tenant NAT pools: customer-specific egress IP ranges can be provisioned; we publish the ranges so customers can lock down corporate firewalls.

2) Failure and degrade behavior
- Fail closed: if an egress gateway fails or becomes unreachable, node-level egress deny rules prevent outbound access until failover completes or manual remediation is performed.

3) Bastion / support access model
- Dedicated management VPC with audited transit. Support access is never left open in tenant subnets.
- Just-in-time (JIT) bastion creation: requested via SSO + MFA, approves by on-call, ephemeral keys provisioned; session recordings and immutable logs retained.
- Audit evidence: session recordings, keystroke logs, and change tickets are available for review under NDA.

Attachments provided: deployment-egress-diagram.svg (high level), egress-rules-summary.pdf (control mappings), bastion-access-table.xlsx (JIT workflow + audit artifacts), SOC2-Type2-Redwood-2026-summary.pdf (compliance summary).
